target_customer: Website owners and marketing teams who load many third-party tools such as analytics and ad pixels
problem: Third-party scripts slow websites and leak data. Zaraz loads them in the cloud through one request, making sites faster and more private.
business_model: SaaS tag manager priced by usage; later a free Cloudflare product

founders.name: Yair Dovrat
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder and CEO in Cloudflare's press release.

founders.name: Yo'av Moshe
founders.background_notes: Listed with Dovrat on the YC page; CTO role from a search summary of secondary sources.

competitors.name: Google Tag Manager
competitors.what: Standard client side tag manager; added server side tagging in August 2020
competitors.traction_then: Default tag manager, no figures found

technical_complexity.rationale: Re-implementing third-party tools server side on edge workers, while keeping their behavior intact, is hard engineering for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Google launched a similar server side container in 2020 and others like Partytown pursued the same performance problem, so the wedge was copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Cloudflare acquired it in December 2021 and made it a Cloudflare product with a free beta; Google shipped server side tagging in 2020.

market_need_then: Third-party scripts hurt Core Web Vitals and privacy, and Cloudflare's own release frames a clear speed and security gap that traditional tag managers could not solve.

branding.domain_note: Owned zaraz.com, which now redirects to a Cloudflare product page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Speed focused; tagline A third-party manager, built for speed

branding.brand_signature: Tagline about a third-party manager built for speed

rebrands.why: Folded into Cloudflare as a product after the acquisition

brand_strength.rationale: A short distinctive name, but no community or brand press beyond product coverage was found.

outcome_analysis: Zaraz solved a real third-party script problem with edge computing and was the first company Cloudflare acquired that was built on Workers, which made it a natural fit. The acquisition came in December 2021, under two years after the Winter 2020 batch, with undisclosed terms. Reported funding of 2 to 3 million dollars is unverified, so the outcome looks like a strategic technology acquisition.
notes: Funding figures (seed of 2 million led by PICO Venture Partners in early 2021, 3 million total on CB Insights, pre-seed from F2 Venture Capital and The Junction) appear only on aggregators and snippets, so no round is recorded; some aggregator pages were mislabeled Sweeps. Google Tag Manager existed before 2020; the source date is the server side launch. CTO role from secondary summaries. YC page lists no education or employers. Cloudflare says it was the first acquisition built on Workers. Completeness pass: the $2M seed is now recorded from a single database (Startupintros, dated May 2020); earlier notes said early 2021 led by PICO, which a search could not confirm, so investors are left empty. CB Insights total of 3M exceeds the recorded round, and the pre-seed from F2 and The Junction has no amount, so the gap stays unrecorded.
